scenes.headline: How Halo routes tokens to experts
scenes.sub: A post-training framework, and where its lead over stock TRL comes from.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bramblewood! Halo trains mixture-of-experts models up to two point eight times faster than stock TRL. Here's where that comes from.

scenes.text: The gap is mostly structural, not kernels: Halo sends each token to the one GPU that owns its expert, instead of summing the full output everywhere.

left.title: Stock transformers
items: Every GPU holds the whole batch
Experts it doesn't own get zero scores
The full output is summed across every GPU
left.say: In stock transformers, every GPU keeps the whole batch, zeroes the experts it doesn't own, and sums the full output across all of them.

right.title: Halo's token routing
items: Each token goes once to its expert's GPU
A grouped matmul runs the local experts
Results return to where they started
right.say: Halo moves tokens instead. Each one travels once to the GPU holding its expert, and comes back to where it started.

steps.say: Each GPU starts with its own tokens. A router, in full precision, picks each token's top experts.
Dispatch sends every token once to the GPU that owns its expert. There, one grouped matrix multiply runs all the local experts.
Combine sends each result home, same rows, same order. Every GPU still trains on its own batch.

steps.note: For gpt-oss-20b, the wire carries 4/32 of the batch per layer
steps.say: So the wire carries each token's share, not a full-tensor sum on every GPU.

steps.label: ZeRO-3: one shard each, re-gathered every micro-step
steps.say: Stock TRL shards every weight eight ways and re-gathers all twenty point seven billion parameters every micro-step.

steps.label: ZeRO-2: every GPU keeps the weights resident
steps.say: Halo's default keeps them resident. More memory, less waiting, and that difference sits inside the two point eight.

scenes.title: Halo over stock TRL, per GPU
scenes.say: Sharded the same way on both sides, Halo still leads: one point two five times at four K, and two point six eight at sixteen K.

scenes.text: It isn't the kernel: even on the slow per-expert loop, Halo beats TRL's grouped GEMM. The lead is structural, routing first.
scenes.say: It isn't the kernel. Even on the slow per-expert loop, Halo beats TRL's fast grouped kernel. The lead is structural, routing first.

recap: Tokens travel to their expert's GPU and back
ZeRO-2 keeps weights resident, part of the 2.8×
scenes.say: To recap: route tokens, don't sum outputs, and know which sharding you're comparing.
